idiom_name: named creation operation (factory method on the aggregate, or a standalone factory) over a non-public validating constructor
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give every creation path its own name from the ubiquitous language and make it the only way in. The factory validates preconditions (including rules that need other aggregates or policies), mints or accepts identity, then calls a constructor that clients cannot reach, so the returned object is valid by construction. Prefer factory methods on the aggregate while construction belongs conceptually to the product and needs no external knowledge; extract a standalone factory when creation must load other aggregates, consult a policy, or translate an external or legacy payload. Return a typed failure rather than a partial object, and keep repositories or services on the factory, never on the product.
pitfalls: Leaving a public constructor next to the factory: the invariant becomes optional and callers bypass the named path.
Letting the factory also persist or commit; creation and transaction ownership are different responsibilities.
Duplicating the same rule in factory and constructor until the two drift; keep the factory about preconditions and the aggregate about state invariants.

Wrong move: silently repair bad input inside the factory (trim, clamp, default a missing field) -> the aggregate looks valid but the caller's data was quietly changed and the real bug never surfaces -> instead reject with a typed failure and let the caller or an anti-corruption layer decide how to coerce.

Wrong move: the factory reads globals, wall-clock time, or singletons (current date, a static repository) instead of receiving collaborators -> every test of a creation path becomes order- and environment-dependent -> instead inject the clock, id generator, and repositories as explicit parameters of the factory.

Wrong move: route state transitions of an already-existing aggregate (confirm, cancel) through the factory because it 'owns creation' -> the factory turns into a switch over lifecycle states and the aggregate loses its own behavioural vocabulary -> instead keep transitions as named methods on the aggregate and reserve the factory for bringing objects into existence, including rehydration.
